current.text: He is the projected starter at shooting guard next to Mikel Brown Jr. in a lineup with Michael Porter Jr., Julius Randle and Day'Ron Sharpe. The Nets do not see him as a full-time point guard. He will play both on and off the ball.
Coach Jordi Fernandez wants several ball handlers and connective playmakers rather than one traditional point guard.
Randle will handle the ball a lot, so Demin will handle it less. At best he is the third offensive option, and his usage should rise only a little, from 19.5 to about 20 or 21.
In summer league he averaged 19 points and 5 assists. He made 76% of about six two-point attempts a game, drove more and hit mid-range shots, but he did not hit his threes.

The Nets see him as an integral piece and expect a leap in his second year as an on-ball creator and interior scorer. That could unlock more pick and roll playmaking. Experts expect more usage and better efficiency.
He finished outside the top 200 last season (230th in categories) while dealing with a foot issue.

Josh projects him around 120th with a wide range and upside to about 80th. That makes him a round 10 to 11 pick. He calls Demin his best upside target in all formats for year two, and others call him a solid late flyer.

Brooklyn projects as one of the worst teams, at about 28 wins. Houston owns its pick, so the Nets have no reason to tank. The front office will likely keep making moves, and Porter is a trade candidate.
The second half of the season is uncertain for Brooklyn. The team could hand more minutes to young players, Demin included, which helps him more than the veterans.
Brooklyn has 16 back-to-backs, tied for the most in the league. With a March 28 end, its playoff schedule is 3-4-3 games with only one back-to-back.

durable.text: As a rookie he was mainly a three-point shooter. He hit 39% on about six threes a game, took only about two twos a game (43%), rarely got to the line and averaged about three assists.
In college at BYU he was a point guard with big passing numbers who could not shoot.
Threes are his best category. His FG% is weak for a guard, so he fits a punt FG% build.
His defensive stats are poor and he is not a big rebounder.

note: Yahoo ranks him 144th at 0 USD and ESPN ranks him 107th at 2 USD, while Josh projects him around 120th with upside near 80th, so he is a 1 to 2 USD end-of-auction buy with breakout upside. He fits punt FG% builds that want threes (about 3.1 per game projected) plus some assists from a guard. Early on, check that he starts, how many twos he takes and whether his FG% climbs from last season's 39.9%. Also watch how much the ball goes to Randle.
